1	# @pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media
2	
3	A PostCSS plugin for theme-aware CSS authoring. It supports both theme custom-idents in media
4	features (for example, `(theme: canvas)`) and `@custom-media --theme-*` aliases, then lowers them
5	to concrete target-theme output.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	```sh
10	npm i -D @pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media postcss
11	```
12	
13	Also available as `pantoken/themeCustomMedia`.
14	
15	## Usage
16	
17	```ts
18	import postcss from "postcss";
19	import { themeCustomMedia } from "@pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media";
20	
21	const out = postcss([themeCustomMedia({ theme: "canvas" })]).process(css, { from: undefined }).css;
22	```
23	
24	## Authoring
25	
26	### Theme custom-idents
27	
28	Author directly with the `theme` media feature:
29	
30	```css
31	@media (theme: canvas) {
32	  .button {
33	    color: blue;
34	  }
35	}
36	
37	@media (theme: rebrand) and (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
38	  .button {
39	    color: white;
40	  }
41	}
42	```
43	
44	For the selected target theme, non-matching theme branches are dropped, matching `theme:*`
45	clauses are removed, and wrappers that become unconditional are unwrapped.
46	
47	### Theme custom-media aliases
48	
49	Author with `@custom-media` aliases and consume them in `@media`:
50	
51	```css
52	@custom-media --theme-canvas (theme: canvas);
53	@custom-media --theme-dark (theme: rebrand) and (prefers-color-scheme: dark);
54	
55	@media (--theme-canvas) {
56	  .button {
57	    color: blue;
58	  }
59	}
60	```
61	
62	Built-in `--theme-*` aliases are expanded before lowering, and emitted CSS removes only
63	`@custom-media --theme-*` declarations. Non-theme aliases are preserved.
64	
65	## Aliases
66	
67	- `--theme-rebrand` -> `(theme: rebrand)`
68	- `--theme-canvas` -> `(theme: canvas)`
69	- `--theme-canvas-high-contrast` -> `(theme: canvasHighContrast)`
70	- `--theme-light` -> `(theme: rebrand) and (prefers-color-scheme: light)`
71	- `--theme-dark` -> `(theme: rebrand) and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`
72	
73	## API
74	
75	- `themeCustomMedia(options?): Plugin` - create the lowering plugin.
76	- default export - `themeCustomMedia`.
77	
78	## License
79	
80	MIT

# Fix: theme-conditional component rules missing from the docs live `@example` previews

## Context

In the VitePress docs, the live `@example` previews have a theme switcher (rebrand / canvas /
canvasHighContrast). Switching themes re-colors token *values* but never applies theme-conditional
*rules*. Concrete symptom in `formats/components/src/components/billboard.css`: the base hover rule
appears in the live site, but its `@media (--theme-canvas), (--theme-canvas-high-contrast)` override
(which swaps `border-color` from `--instui-color-text-base` to `--instui-component-link-text-color`)
never shows, in any theme.

**The custom-media plugin is not broken.** `@pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media`
(`plugins/postcss/theme-custom-media/src/index.ts`) is a *build-time* resolver by design: for a
target theme it prunes every non-matching `@media (--theme-*)` branch and unwraps the survivor,
emitting concrete single-theme CSS. `formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts` runs it per
theme and exports `billboard = billboardByTheme.rebrand` as the default, so
`formats/components/generated/components.css` (copied to `demos-assets/components.css`) is the
**rebrand** sheet with the canvas block already pruned.

The docs switch themes at **runtime** by toggling `<html data-pantoken-theme>`
(`docs/.vitepress/theme/theme.ts:74` `applyTheme`), which only re-scopes token *values* via
`site-themes.css`. `billboard`'s theme rule changes which *token* is referenced — a different rule,
not a different value — so the attribute toggle has nothing to activate. `billboard.css` is the only
file in the repo using `@media (--theme-*)` today.

**Intended outcome:** the docs load a single `components.css` that carries all three themes' rules at
once — rebrand rules unscoped, canvas/canvasHighContrast rules scoped under
`:root[data-pantoken-theme="…"]` — mirroring exactly what `docs/scripts/site-themes.ts` already does
for token values. The existing attribute toggle then activates the right rules. The published
`@pantoken/components` package keeps emitting per-theme concrete sheets, unchanged.

## Approach (docs-local, chosen)

Generate the multi-theme sheet in the docs pipeline, reusing `componentsCss` from
`@pantoken/components`. Do **not** touch the plugin, `component-styles.ts`, the record files, or the
published package output/deps.

Key fact that makes this clean: `themeCustomMedia` never resolves `var()`, so the only difference
